page: Amazon Web Services m8id.32xlarge is an eighth-generation general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors running at up to 3.9 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 128 dedicated vCPUs across 64 physical cores with multithreading enabled, supported by a 480 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 512.0 GB of high-frequency DDR5 memory, maintaining a balanced 4:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The configuration includes 7,600 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage and offers a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. No dedicated GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark evaluations highlight exceptional throughput in highly parallelized compute and memory-intensive tasks. The system scores in the top tier for multi-core stress-ng execution, multi-core Geekbench processing, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Hardware acceleration flags such as AMX and AVX-512 facilitate top-tier results in extended CPU instructions, encryption, and PassMark database operations. In data-serving tests, the instance achieves top-tier outcomes with 210.58 million operations per second in Redis SET commands and 206.31 GB/sec in static web serving, alongside rapid prompt processing for large language models.

From an architectural standpoint, the combination of high-density compute cores, fast DDR5 channels, and massive integrated NVMe storage yields high operational efficiency for I/O-heavy environments. The primary tradeoff lies in single-core performance, which ranks in the average range compared to specialized compute-focused instances, and the lack of discrete GPUs for accelerated training. Consequently, this server is optimal for distributed relational and NoSQL databases, large-scale CI/CD build farms, static web hosting clusters, and enterprise-grade ETL pipelines that demand massive local caching and high core counts.
description: Amazon Web Services m8id.32xlarge is a high-density, general-purpose server powered by Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors on the Nitro hypervisor. The instance features 128 dedicated vCPUs, 512.0 GB of DDR5 memory, a 480 MB L3 cache, and 7,600 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, backed by 50 Gbps baseline network throughput. Operating without discrete GPUs, it relies on advanced vector and matrix extensions (AVX-512, AMX) to accelerate compute tasks. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier execution in multi-core processing, multi-threaded decompression, database transactions, and in-memory key-value operations like Redis. While single-thread speeds represent a moderate middle-tier profile, the platform delivers strong resource density and I/O capability, making it well matched for high-concurrency databases, large-scale enterprise microservices, real-time analytics, and data-intensive ETL workflows.
